You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: continual-arc-motif-stamping
description: Use for ARC grids with a colored pixel motif embedded in noisy background. Detect and stamp exact translations of that motif.
---

# Continual ARC motif stamping

Use when input has a mostly uniform background color, scattered contrasting pixels, and one or more connected clusters in a distinct motif color; examples may show that motif recolored at many matching locations.

1. Preserve the input grid exactly as the starting output.
2. Identify the motif color (the marked cluster color) and background color. Extract the motif's colored-cell coordinates, then normalize by subtracting minimum row and column to get offsets.
3. Enumerate every in-bounds translation of the motif bounding box. A translation qualifies only if **every motif-offset cell in the original input is background color**. Do not allow existing motif-color cells or arbitrary non-background cells to satisfy a candidate; this causes false placements.
4. For each qualifying placement, recolor only those motif-offset cells to the motif color. Keep all other cells unchanged. Overlapping qualifying placements simply union their recolored cells.
5. Submit same-size grid. Verify dimensions, and confirm marked seed pixels/background/unrelated cells were not altered.

The motif may be irregular and can have holes within its bounding box; only the colored offsets are tested. Learn color and motif anew from each task's demos rather than carrying colors or coordinates across instances.",
